name: ssplayer-for-react-native
description: SpriteStudio player for React Native — workspace root
//scripts: Every entry point is a .js shim that picks the .sh or .ps1 implementation
for the host OS (scripts/run-platform-script.js) — naming a .sh here would
shut Windows contributors out. Same shape as SSPlayerForWeb.
check-framedata is macOS/Linux-only on purpose: it is a developer guard
that needs flatc and a host cargo build, not part of any build path.
check-mask is macOS-only for the same kind of reason: it links the host
libskia RN Skia ships, which has no Linux slice.
check-hidden needs neither flatc nor Skia — only a host cargo build — so it
is the cheapest of the three to run.
check-web-barrel is plain node rather than a .sh/.ps1 pair, and needs no
Brain at all: nothing in it is platform-specific, so a shim would only shut
Windows contributors out of the one check they could otherwise run.
generate-fbs-code takes out=<dir> so check-framedata can
regenerate into a scratch dir and diff, rather than reimplementing it.
build names the package rather than `pnpm -r`: docs has a
build too, and it is typedoc + vitepress, already reachable as `docs`.
build-release writes the tarball into release-dist/ and re-opens it, and
uploads nothing. It runs anywhere; `release` is the same run with the draft
GitHub Release on the end, and is macOS-only.
prepare-docs and build-docs are the family-standard docs pair; docs and
docs:dev stay as the raw workspace passthrough build-docs itself calls.
The docs need no Brain: typedoc reads TypeScript, vitepress reads markdown.
run-ios has no .ps1: it needs macOS and Xcode anyway.
